As long as I've had a Steam account (a couple years, give or take), PvP games and competitive shooters have eluded me. The mix of confusion and frustration made the experience a miasma of exhaustion and regret.

That is, until I played The Finals.
This game's combination of unique gameplay mechanics, cohesive art direction, and strategic resources make the experience truly one-of-a-kind. The degree of variety in this game allows a large amount of effective strategies, incentivizing experimentation. I have personally workshopped multiple loadouts that end up getting results after enough practice.

The game's art direction is also very solid. Unlike other prominent free-to-play shooters (Team Fortress 2, Overwatch, etc.), The Finals takes its art style in a more realistic direction, allowing for a more digestible visual experience. This helps me as someone who has trouble identifying the difference between an enemy player and set dressing.

The wide variety of weapons and gadgets available in this game also helped me acclimate to this gameplay environment. Meta options are a constant in PvP shooters, but The Finals manages to tweak balance in order to make sure those options don't completely suffocate the more fun or alternative tools available.

Finding success with non-traditional weapons gives me a lot of satisfaction. As someone who generally struggles with long range options (sniper rifles, bows, etc.), I appreciate being able to do well in a match. As frustrating as playing "sniper peek-a-boo" may be, I find countering snipers to be way easier in this game than in other shooters.

The destructible buildings, the game's central mechanic, keep the gameplay unpredictable and exciting. Camping on rooftops or in isolated rooms is no longer a viable long-term strategy, forcing players to engage with each other as the flow of battle leaves a sea of destruction in its wake. Revisiting areas where fights have taken place earlier in a match is also a really cool experience.

Long story short, I recommend The Finals for both shooter game veterans and gamers getting introduced to the genre. The unique gameplay manages to keep the blow-by-blow experience exciting and refreshing. Give this game a shot, you won't regret it!

I see a lot of people complaining about the new update, but I don't get it. As a loyal medium main for around 300 hours of my 400, I understand why people can find lights annoying, or the game unbalanced. But to be completely honest, there is so much you can do to counter these issues. I personally find only one thing deplorable and that is sword mains, but honestly annoying experiences from these types of players are far and few between for me at least. Sure they changed a few things, they may have not made the best balancing decisions but at least in QC I don't see too much of a difference gameplay wise. 

In the Finals the only limit to your strategies is your imagination. Want to collapse a six story building from the ground up with a sledgehammer that drops everyone fighting over objective? You can do it. Want to take a chair, place turrrets on it and run around with an autoturret? You can do it. Want to collapse an entire bridge into a void along with an enemy team? Guess what, you can do that. 

Performance wise, this game runs pretty well. On lower end devices like my friends Ryzen 5 1600 and GTX 1050, 60fps on low is achieveable, and on my device (specs attached) I get a stable 120fps on comp settings. Be warned though, that this game is CPU heavy, so that will be your bottleneck. If I had a better CPU (e.g a Ryzen 5 5600x) I would probably be getting over 180fps by my estimations. 

Just give it a shot, this game is free, you have nothing to lose at all. Only to gain.

I've been primarily a **Valorant player**, occasionally playing games like PUBG and Apex Legends. Recently, one of my friends suggested that I try **THE FINALS**, so I started playing it with him. Honestly, I didn't expect much at first, but I absolutely love this game.

The biggest reason I enjoy THE FINALS is that it feels genuinely different. It's not the same gameplay loop repeated over and over again. In games like Valorant, you're essentially playing around the same objective every match: planting and defusing the bomb, learning maps, holding angles, and anticipating enemy movements. On top of that, players tend to gravitate towards a handful of popular agents and repeatedly use similar strategies. While there's obviously a competitive depth to that, I personally find it somewhat repetitive and stagnating after playing for a long time.

THE FINALS, on the other hand, feels unpredictable. The destructible environments completely change how matches play out. Buildings collapsing, walls being blown apart, unexpected engagements and constantly changing situations make every match feel different. I also love how you can adapt your approach by switching classes, changing your equipment and adjusting your loadout depending on what the opposing team is doing. It makes the gameplay feel dynamic rather than predictable.

Compared to battle royale games like Apex Legends, Fortnite and PUBG, I personally find THE FINALS much more refreshing. Battle royale has been around for almost a decade, and although those games are still enjoyable, I feel like the genre has become somewhat oversaturated. It's refreshing to see a shooter trying something different rather than following an established formula.

Honestly, I consider THE FINALS one of the best FPS games out there right now. What I genuinely don't understand is why this game doesn't have a much larger player base. It has so much potential, an incredibly fun gameplay loop and something that many other shooters are missing: unpredictability.

I would genuinely recommend people give this game a try. If you're getting tired of playing the same shooters with the same objectives and repetitive gameplay loops, **THE FINALS is absolutely worth playing.**

It's a shame I decided to give The Finals a thumbs down. Here's my experience as of this review.

[h1] Positives: [/h1]
Chances are you came here from a Kelski video, so I won't go into all the positives. The game's concept is fun, there are multiple game modes, in-depth character customization, and destructible environments.

[h1] Negatives: [/h1]
The playerbase.
- Skill gap
- Guaranteed Losses
- Smurfs
- Cheaters

[h2] Skill gap [/h2]
There is a huge skill gap between new players and experienced players. The matches when you get the perfect middle ground where everyone is roughly the same skill level where it's anyone's guess on who will win as every team snatches a small victory from the jaws of defeat until the match ends are the best. However, the middle ground is almost nonexistent with heavily lopsided teams with a team filled with super-duper-unemployed-y-y-slide-cancel-extraordinaries and the other filled with literal noobs with only a few hours played. It's difficult to learn how to play a game when you're constantly getting eliminated to the point of being spawn camped or completely destroyed by other teams. 

There is a bot mode (which only allows the Cashout mode) "to help new players learn the game," but it can only go so far as you quickly learn how the bots play and what paths they take on each map; this doesn't help you against other players. There's also a limited amount of bot maps with limited features so you won't learn about map elements like weather, floating platforms, and moving platforms.

There's also an odd lack of advice. While many players don't have mics or type in chat, the ones that do usually only complain. They don't bother giving tips or suggesting strategies. I had a match which ended under 5 minutes with no objectives taken only for one guy, at the game over screen, complain about how terrible the team was. Never during that 5 minutes did he make any suggestions on how to approach the objectives, do callouts of where enemies were, or anything that may help the team improve.

Retaining new players is difficult if the game isn't fun and/or if there feels like there is no sign of improving, which can lead to new players leaving, thus making the skill gap issue worse.

Edit: [h2] Guaranteed Losses [/h2]
Players often leave after the match has started nearly instantly if the match does not go the way they THINK it is going. This is a major problem because the major-sweatlord-gamemodes (the core gamemodes) do not allow players to join a match that is in progress. This means once one or both players leave your team, the "maybe" loss has become a guaranteed loss. It becomes ONLY YOU versus the entire lobby until the match ends.

You can leave the match early if you want, but that means (according to the Yes-No message asking if you want to leave mid-match) no progress, no rewards, and a potential "penalty" added to your account.

[h2] Smurfs [/h2]
Smurfs don't help with the skill gap issue. Experienced players can and do make new accounts so they can be at a low level and destroy noobs.  Now, a new player may get lucky with a TF2-style triple backstab, but low level accounts with default outfits pulling such moves constantly are obviously not noobs. Same goes for players with near inhuman-level aim and recoil control, which leads to the next issue.

[h2] Cheaters [/h2]
Yes, there are cheaters in The Finals, no matter how hard people deny it. Yes, every online competitive game has cheaters, but the number and frequency of cheaters in The Finals is high. There's the typical aimbot where every shot lands perfectly with no recoil -- one egregious instance had a bow & arrow player constantly flick to me and land every shot on me across buildings throughout the match -- and wallhacks -- two different players in two different matches aimed at me through walls while I was cloaked (invisibility gadget) and not moving (no sound) yet both followed me perfectly and killed me while I was invisible; there were no spotting gadgets used.

If you still want to download and play, I highly recommend going into the settings and turning on the "Instant Replay" killcam; it's off by default. This makes it easier to spot cheaters' suspicious behavior to report, but also gives good insight on how honest, non-cheating good players play. Also, periodically check to see if the "Instant Replay" option is still on because sometimes it won't play.

The destruction, the chaos, the movement, the objective play. It ignited something in me that I didn't realize I was missing. After my first session, I was hooked. I started playing in July and have already put more than 500 hours into it.

That said, you should know what you're getting into.

This is a sweaty game.

You're going to get destroyed for a while before things start clicking. Even after that, you'll still lose and die a lot. The upside is that success feels incredibly rewarding. Every kill feels earned, and every win feels like hitting the lottery. If you're playing with friends, those moments become even better.

[b]The Pros[/b]

[h2]Destruction[/h2]

The destruction is the first thing you'll notice, and it's arguably the best in the business.

Blowing holes through floors to ambush opponents, collapsing buildings onto objective sites, or tossing an explosive canister into a random structure just because you can never gets old. The destruction isn't a gimmick. It's a core part of the gameplay, and it changes the way every match unfolds.

[h2]Skill Expression[/h2]

This is where The Finals really shines.

There are three classes, multiple specializations, dozens of gadgets, different weapons, and countless ways to approach fights and objectives. You can build a character that genuinely matches your personality and playstyle.

More importantly, the skill ceiling is absurdly high. Hundreds of hours later and I'm still learning new things everyday.

[h2]Cosmetics[/h2]

The cosmetic system is excellent.

You can create anything from a tactical operator to the most cursed abomination imaginable. Few games give players this much freedom to customize their characters.

A lot of the best cosmetics are paid, but the sheer variety on display is impressive.

[b]The Cons[/b]

[h2]Server Issues and Desync[/h2]

Because destruction is server-side and must remain synchronized for every player, desync occasionally becomes part of the experience.

You'll sometimes run into questionable hit registration, delayed actions, or moments where things simply don't line up the way they should. It's frustrating, but never quite bad enough to make me quit.

[h2]Cheaters and Smurfs[/h2]

They're here.

Like most free-to-play competitive shooters, you'll encounter cheaters and smurfs from time to time. It's an unfortunate reality of the genre.

[h2]Balance[/h2]

Balance is a constant work in progress.

Some updates are excellent. Others leave you scratching your head and wondering what the developers were thinking. The game is rarely unplayable because of balance issues, but confusing balance decisions are a recurring frustration.

[h2]Brutal Learning Curve[/h2]

This is probably the biggest hurdle for new players.

The player population isn't huge, which means you'll frequently run into veterans who know the game inside and out. On top of that, The Finals doesn't play like most shooters.

If you approach it like Call of Duty, you're going to struggle.

At its core, this is a team-based objective game. Kills matter, but winning objectives matters more. A great K/D doesn't necessarily translate into victories if you aren't helping your team.

I suspect this is one of the main reasons many new players bounce off the game.

[b]Final Thoughts[/b]

The most important thing to remember is that this game is completely free.

You can spend zero dollars and still have essentially the full gameplay experience. While cosmetics are a big part of the fun, there's no paywall preventing you from competing.

Despite its flaws, The Finals has become one of my favorite multiplayer games ever made. The destruction, skill expression, and sheer unpredictability create moments that no other FPS can replicate.

If any of that sounds appealing to you, it's absolutely worth downloading and trying for yourself.

I have done ranked a few times previous seasons and I have achieved a rank I am happy with- which is Diamond 1 and I will no longer touch ranked. 

Now for the meat of the review

Season 12, Thought it was great at first but it is riddled with so many bugs AND cheaters. I've been playing since beta and finally sat down to write this. The game is amazing in its own way, but recent updates have been frustrating.

Some of the melee reworks are solid, but certain scenarios make getting kills nearly impossible. Getting hit with the goo gun, shockwave, and kicks while someone is using a heal beam shuts you down completely.

The new destructibility is a step backward. Traversing the destruction is clunky and unreliable. Floors dip just enough that you can't run up them, and you get stuck half the time. The rubber-banding while climbing is especially bad—it feels straight out of Battlefield, which tracks given the shared developers. The new menu even looks like a Battlefield menu.

They should fix traversal and movement through destruction before adding more of it. Right now the obstacles make the game feel worse, not better.

True Sight and Smoke together are overpowered. and the Medium sonar grenade just turns matches into a constant spotting fest. Explosives only break smoke for a second before it reforms perfectly. Revert the old smoke timer and make more tools properly disperse it: explosives, shockwave, and maybe the Slam in Charge and Slam.

Invisibility is a nightmare now with all the new gadgets. It's not unusable, but sneaking with a knife feels impossible. The ability drains too fast and you lose half of it on activation. Too many things counter it, especially if sonar grenade stays on Medium. Revert it to the old version of Invisibility.

Medium’s APS turret needs a range buff to deal with smokes and the Heavy grenade launcher buff. The constant back-and-forth of buffing and nerfing things instead of properly balancing around them is exhausting.

[h1]Fun core gameplay, but the progression and cosmetics are underwhelming.[/h1]
The gameplay is reasonably fun. You fight over objectives and blow stuff up, and the destruction is the best part: you can take down big chunks of buildings and the map, so the same location can be approached in completely different ways. It runs well in most situations, though it can stutter when a lot of destruction is happening at once.

Some of the people working on this game are making really good use of the new tools available to them. The devs openly say they use text-to-speech for the commentators Scotty & June, and a recent addition is that plays you make, good or bad, can cause them to call out your player name, which feels great. Loving that.

[h2]Season 12 locked bot players out of progression.[/h2]
The playerbase is fairly small and experienced, so it's easy to run into people far better than you or your friends, which can make new shooter players quit on the spot. The bot mode was a great fix for that and was how I played with my friends. But since the season 12 update, contracts no longer progress in Cashout (Bots). I tested it myself, and the ones I wanted to complete didn't progress at all. That means the people I enjoyed playing with most can't advance their accounts anymore. Some lack experience or skill, and some have disabilities that limit how they perform against the average player, but they do fine against bots. Their choices are now to play normal matches where they get endlessly outperformed and have a miserable time, or to stop playing. A few of my friends have just quit.

[h2]Cosmetics: limited, expensive, and uneven in quality.[/h2]
Character customization is a fun and important way for me to express myself, and it matters even more here than in other shooters, because your character is front and center at the start of every match, and again at the end if you do well. Not being able to customize my character the way I want is the main reason I'm enjoying the game less and less. The parts I'd need are either limited edition, temporarily locked, or simply don't exist. The selection of faces and hairstyles is extremely disappointing. There are some interesting body paints and tattoos, but most outfits cover so much that you never get to show them off.

What I'm being sold is mostly low-to-mediocre quality cosmetics, and all of it, even the mediocre stuff, is priced at a premium, not just the occasional good one. Some assets clearly look like they were made with generative AI, with visible inconsistencies, though I can't tell to what degree. To be clear, I don't have a problem with generative AI itself. If it makes the devs' work easier or gives us features that wouldn't otherwise be possible, like the commentators calling out our names, great. But if what I get is bad quality at a premium price, I'm not buying it, and if they keep shoveling it at me, there's a point where I'm fed up enough that I'll just leave.

What I passionately dislike is being sold a recolor of a hairstyle I already own instead of an actual new hairstyle. Sure, a new hairstyle is more work for the devs, but that work is what shows me they give a shit. I also don't want to own the same hairstyle 4-5 times in different colors. I want it once, and then I pick whichever unlocked color I feel like using. With how things are priced at a premium, I have to decide each time whether to buy an entire new game or part of an outfit. It makes me want to scream, because it tells me that whoever is in charge of setting the prices, or whoever approved them, has entirely lost touch with what money is worth.

[h2]Body types make female characters feel like an afterthought.[/h2]
It's hard to tell which body types are meant to be male or female, since they all look like male models with minor adjustments. That makes creating cool/badass or cute female characters very limiting to impossible.

THE FINALS – One of the Most Fun and Addictive Multiplayer Games I've Ever Played

THE FINALS is genuinely one of those games that reminds me why I love multiplayer gaming in the first place. In a market filled with repetitive shooters that often feel like copies of one another, THE FINALS manages to stand out with its own identity, offering an experience that feels fresh, chaotic, creative, and incredibly fun.

What makes this game so special is its unique gameplay and mechanics. The fully destructible environments completely change the way you approach every match. Buildings can collapse, walls can be blown apart, floors can disappear, and entire strategies can change within seconds. There is something incredibly satisfying about destroying an entire building just to eliminate an enemy team or completely changing the battlefield to your advantage. The level of environmental destruction adds a layer of unpredictability that very few shooters can offer.

The movement, gunplay, gadgets, abilities, and different character builds make the gameplay even more interesting. Every match feels like a different experience because there are so many ways to approach a situation. You can play aggressively, support your teammates, set traps, defend objectives, or come up with completely unexpected strategies. The freedom to experiment with different loadouts and playstyles keeps things exciting and prevents the gameplay from becoming stale.

But honestly, the biggest achievement of THE FINALS is just how FUN it is. The chaotic team fights, last-second objective steals, unexpected comebacks, insane destruction, and those perfectly timed plays create moments that are genuinely memorable. Even when a match doesn't go your way, there's almost always something entertaining happening.

And that's probably my favourite thing about this game: I KEEP COMING BACK TO IT. No matter how many hours I put into it, I never seem to get bored. I can take a break, come back after a while, and still have just as much fun as I did when I first started playing. It has that rare quality where you tell yourself you'll play just one more match, and suddenly hours have passed.

THE FINALS isn't perfect, and like every multiplayer game, it has its flaws. But its creativity, unique identity, incredible destruction mechanics, and sheer entertainment value make it stand out from the crowd.

I genuinely appreciate what Embark Studios has created here. It's not just another competitive FPS; it's a game that encourages creativity, rewards experimentation, and constantly creates unpredictable moments.

If you ask me, THE FINALS is one of the most entertaining multiplayer shooters out there, and I honestly hope this game continues to grow. I don't see myself getting tired of it anytime soon.

[h1] Wasted Potential [/h1]

Let me start off by saying that I've been playing The Finals since it first launched on day 1. It's such a unique game compared to other online shooters on the market, both in gameplay and aesthetics. I remember playing Season 1 so much, it was similar to how engrossing Elden Ring was when it first came out. Every season I would buy the battle pass and other standalone cosmetics hoping to support the game so it would stick around and mature. It has been my favorite game, by far, for the last several years.

Unfortunately the game has been declining in quality since Season 11, and now Season 12 has now made playing it such a miserable experience that I leave feeling angry and cheated, rather than having had any fun at all.


[h3] Broken Balance Changes [/h3]
Every online shooter has balance changes, we all know this. It's how the developers maintain a balance for all players to have a fair experience as features get added / removed from the game. Embark has, unfortunately, seriously dropped the ball here. They have essentially "vanilla-fied" each class's attributes so that they no longer feel like a unique playstyle from one another. A handful of weapons have been buffed significantly, while the rest remain collecting dust as they have been rendered utterly useless in medium to high-skill play.

This "vanillafication" of the game has ultimately produced a handful of meta builds that produce extremely successful results, while the rest essentially handicap you to act as killstreak fodder for the top performing team in the lobby.

[h3] Complex UI Layouts [/h3]
You know how companies like Apple constantly feel the need to change their UI around solely to make them feel new, forcing you to re-learn where they put all the settings and icons you used to have memorized? Yeah, that's how Season 12 feels now.

The developers took what was once a clean, functional, UI system that was easy to navigate, and rearranged everything into nested menu schemas for no reason other than to frustrate the player. Hovering over items in your loadout now produces a giant text box that blocks all the other items so you can't view your entire kit at once. Challenge progress trackers have been removed from the scoreboard, so you can no longer tell how close you are to meeting a goal in the middle of a game. Some menus require you to tab left / right to cycle through them, while others require you to manually scroll left / right without any intuitive reason why.

[h3] Lackluster Sponsors / Lore [/h3]
Nearly all of the Sponsors that used to be available for players to sign up with have been removed from the game, aside from OSPUZE, IISEUL-T, and ALFA ACTA. If you were in the middle of progressing through a previous sponsor's career track, I guess it sucks to be you.

Embark claimed they were re-working the sponsorships so that they would be a more engaging part of the game, rather than just a series of side quests. Well, I hate to break it to you, but they are still exactly the same thing: only now with less sponsors to choose from, a disorganized UI for the challenge menus, and a "coach" character that basically sits in the UI menu and yaps nonsense in your ear in a feeble attempt to create game lore. They remind me of AI-generated art and voiceovers that you would find in a cringe anime gatcha game.

[h3] Pointless Destruction Rework [/h3]
Environmental destruction has always been one of the calling cards that made The Finals unique, and added enough novelty into each game so no two matches felt the same. Unfortunately, Embark has clearly never heard the expression "Don't fix what isn't broken!" ( pun intended ). Previously, building would collapse in larger, solid chunks that added just enough chaos to the environment without making it visually overwhelming. Unfortunately, they have now implemented a new system that basically makes crumbling buildings and structures feel like they are held together with gum. Walls, floors, and ceiling sag instead of collapse, fragile items like ziplines and ladders now take 10x the damage to break for whatever reason, and piles of debris now spawn everywhere under collapsing structures in what seems to be a direct attempt to lower players' frame rates for no beneficial reason whatsoever.

If you played the game long enough before, destruction was a force you learned how to predict so you could use it to your advantage. Now, it seems like every building can take the same damage as your average Dark Souls boss, until it eventually wobbles into a crumbling mess like dried-out Jello.

[h3] Cash-Grab Battle Pass [/h3]
The Season 12 Battle Pass lacks any coherent theme found in previous seasons, both in the cosmetics and other rewards. It's a random amalgamation of half-baked cosmetics that seem to shout "OOOH PLEASE BUY ME BECAUSE IM SHINY" rather than because they are genuinely interesting to look at or even merge well with other outfit items in your library. Embark seems to have also abandoned their core retrofuturism / cyberpunk aesthetic for their cosmetics and now make seemingly random outfits that might sell if you have cash to burn for no reason.

[h3] Matchmaking Blues [/h3]
You're more likely to match with a 10/10 girl on Tinder than you are to get a teammate with two brain cells to rub together in The Finals. I'm about a level 150 with around 30k kills, and I consistently get matched with two teammates who are under level 20 and have less than 5k kills. Yet somehow we seem to get matched up against full squads of Ruby-rank players with 60k+ kills...

Smurf accounts, cheaters, and hacking exasperate this problem even more, as you'll often key two-shot by a "level 3" Light with a bow who seems to have magnets in their mouse. Yet somehow these smurfs are never on your team...



[h1] TLDR [/h1]
[b] If you are an unemployed individual reeking of BO, or a kid in school who can sink 6+ hours a day into grinding away at this game, you'll feel right at home here.

For the rest of us normal humans who want a casually-competitive online shooter experience that doesn't raise your blood pressure, you need not play this game. It ( like many others before ) has unfortunately lost it's original spark and has become a cesspit of microtransactions and broken patch management by obtuse developers. [/b]

Embark seems completely incapable of balancing The Finals. Every balance pass feels like it makes certain weapons or classes worse without actually addressing the underlying problems. Instead of improving the overall state of the game, the changes often feel like unnecessary nerfs that make the gameplay less enjoyable. The Respec Order and melee rework are prime examples of spreadsheet balancing: changes that might look reasonable on paper but clearly weren't evaluated properly in actual gameplay. It honestly feels like the developers don't even understand their own balance data, let alone how their changes affect the game in practice.

Matchmaking is in an absolutely abysmal state. Smurfs and sweats are everywhere, and matches increasingly feel less like competitive games and more like exhausting fights against players who either massively outperform the lobby or deliberately play below their actual skill level. The result is an inconsistent and frustrating experience that makes it difficult to enjoy the game, especially when matchmaking fails to create reasonably balanced matches. A competitive game needs matchmaking that makes winning feel earned and losing feel fair, not a system that regularly throws players into miserable games.

I was perfectly fine with Embark experimenting with AI for the in-game commentators. It's an interesting use of the technology that serves a functional purpose and fits the game's presentation. But AI-generated cosmetics are a completely different matter. They look cheap, lack the care and artistic identity that make cosmetics worth buying, and feel like a shortcut to producing content rather than a genuine creative effort. Cosmetics should be something players want because of their design and personality, not something that looks mass-produced by an algorithm. Using AI for commentator technology was an interesting experiment; using it to produce cosmetics just feels lazy and disappointing.

Overall, it feels like Embark is losing sight of what makes The Finals enjoyable. Balance changes should improve gameplay, matchmaking should respect players' time, and cosmetics should demonstrate creativity and quality. Right now, too many decisions seem to be making the experience worse rather than better.

If you're the kind of person who doesn't mind losing tons and tons of games as you get better, getting obliterated by players infinitely better than you over and over and over again, then if you can stick it out, you'll be part of a competitive community of players that are surprisingly kind of chill. (I gave a message on The Finals Reddit and they were all encouraging), if that's the case, I recommend this to you.

However, if you're a player that can't handle losing multiple games in a row with pretty much almost no chance of winning for a while as you climb the mountainous skill ceiling in order to get better, then i really cannot recommend this game.

Great Gameplay, Overwhelming Experience....

The Good: The Finals is easily one of the best free-to-play FPS games out there. The movement, gunplay, and overall mechanics are excellent. It’s also completely free, with no pay-to-win elements. If you can handle the chaos, it’s a fantastic shooter.

The Bad: For players who prefer clean gunplay and a straightforward FPS experience, The Finals can be exhausting.

The main menu feels like an overcrowded digital shopping mall. The moment you boot it up, you're bombarded with pop-ups, Battle Pass promos, daily challenges, "Store Bundle of the Week" ads, event notifications, and endless XP pop-ups. On top of that, you're occasionally forced into tutorials or intro sequences you never asked for just to get into a match.

The gameplay itself isn’t much better in this regard. Between constant commentary, bright cashout indicators, flashy effects, explosions, and destructible environments, there’s simply too much happening on screen at once. What should make the game exciting often becomes overwhelming.

Verdict: Personally, I find the game unplayable. After around 10 minutes or just two or three short matches, I experience severe sensory overload, mental fatigue, and headaches. There’s just too much visual and audio clutter.

If you enjoy fast-paced, chaotic shooters, you’ll probably love it. But if you value visual clarity, simplicity, and pure gunplay, be warned: The Finals can be seriously overwhelming.

I love this game. Its design is beautiful, cosmetics are so dope, the classes require you to work as a team, and quick cash was the first game mode and still the gold mine for casual players.
But over time this game has gotten destroyed with "balances". 
I understand the dynamic and needs for changes for comp mode, bc lights tend to fall short objectively, but for casual play, lights have always been a dominating force, especially against an uncoordinated team. It took Embark over a year to finally say, oh wow melee needs a change bc lights have been DEMOLISHING us with swords the entire time bc they have 3 dashes and 2 ways of going invisible. (the invisibility is the strongest visual effect I've ever seen in a PvP game, i think thats been worked on recently, but still strong. They should only have one way to go invis, and it should just be their spec, not a gadget.)
And as soon as they take away some of lights power (like finally reducing dashes to 2, which was needed for a long time) you give them other extreme abilities. Their weapons are just outright too strong. If you're going to give them various ways to sneak around, then their weapons should only be effective at very close range. Meanwhile I get sniped by throwing knives and smgs just because they have good recoil control. They also have a very effective healing gun, which once again, just takes away the identity of classes. Embark is one objective tool away from having a double or triple light meta. 
I know it just sounds like this is all aimed at lights... but it is tbh. Mediums have an obvious role, and Heavy's kit is exactly what it should be, and they both have ways of securing the obj... while lights job is just to harass people. Instead of giving them more power and ways to harass people, give them tools that actually apply to obj rather than the gateway... which is literally the only one they have.
Maybe I'm just old now, my reflexes aren't as fast as they used to be, but i just simply can't keep up with the obnoxious  and scattered movement that lights have, along with them being invis the whole time.

[b]The most refreshing take on a shooter, you didn't expect from a F2P game.[/b]

The balance between chaos and skill expression is just right. It already feels fun to play from your first match, until hundreds of hours of gameplay later; something that many popular competitive games struggle with. Also, the 3 classes offer many different ways to synergize with your teammates, but they don't lock you in specific combos, the way hero shooters and MOBAs do.

The destruction system is not just a satisfying gimmick, but a well-polished core mechanic that makes the game stand out from other shooters with destructible buildings. The level design is exceptional, too. Although you might not notice immediately, there is a door exactly where you would expect it, cover where it should be, open space where you should take a risk. Combine all that with wide customization and very-fast-paced action and every session feels like an adventure. The setting of a game show, with crowds cheering, makes every kill feel more intense and justifies the event announcements, which amplifies immersion.

There are some annoying but tolerable flaws worth mentioning. Requiring shaders to recompile after every weekly update is a bold choice. The dagger is a match-breaking weapon in the wrong hands. Also, the commentators' voices are AI, which is quite disappointing...

Overall, this is a game with top of the line game design and great attention to detail. If you play FPSs, you need it in your collection. If you don't, you might after you try this. I recommend [b]Quick Cash[/b] as the best mode.

A wonderful game, with wonderful visuals and wonderful gameplay. Why, then, is this a negative review?

The microtransactions are unreasonably, exorbitantly expensive.
1. Terrible monetization. While the game isn't "pay-to-win"—which is a huge plus, BUT there’s a catch: over 90% of the skins either cost real money or require hundreds upon hundreds of hours of grinding.

3. The player base is very small and falls into two categories: "monsters" who wipe you out in a fraction of a second, and people who are playing the game for the very first (and last) time. As a result, my win rate when playing with random teammates hovers around 10%; it’s simply difficult to perform well alongside randoms when you’re up against a coordinated team of three communicating via Discord.
4. The game has an extremely high barrier to entry. I personally enjoy playing it, but the difficulty is off the charts. While that’s not a drawback for me, at least three of my friends gave up on the game because of it.

To sum it all up: this is a unique, distinctive project that offers a truly one-of-a-kind gaming experience. However, it suffers from several serious flaws that could lead to its demise if the developers don’t take action.
That’s all I wanted to say. Have a great day to everyone reading this, and I hope the developers can restore the game to its former glory.

Marvel Rivals is it af. It is a team based game, so if you aren't giving value on Spiderman and the healers on your team have more kills while your other DPS has double the amount of kills you have: PUT THE MASK DOWN. DPS has too many characters for you to be throwing like that. There are two other roles to explore. The easiest to play is DPS, though. It is the most saturated role. Don't be intimidated by the tank and healing roles even though they are more difficult. 
Quick matches are perfect for learning how teams work without the pressure of playing the game correct. If you aren't a fan of the team-based mode there are multiple other modes you can play. 18v18, while still a team, it's more of a very disorganized team, so you can pop off as much as you want and really get to learn your character. There are also seasonal modes that are PvE and change the abilities of whichever characters they choose to represent that mode (usually male characters), and that can be a blast.
And if playing with people isn't what you want to be doing, you can solo queue most of the seasonal PvE or create your own custom games with BOTs on your team (it's not all that different from playing with real people tbh).
But this game has a lot to offer and I hope it keeps getting better and better.

This game is just miserable. There are some good things, but it's mostly bad.

Overall Game Balance:
This game's balance is horrendous. Every character does way too much, nearly every new character becomes extremely overbearing and extremely difficult to counter. These sort of games have three types of roles. Brawl which are characters that thrive in fights where everything is in close quarters. Dive characters which are characters that focus on quick assassinations and flanks. Poke which are characters that thrive in long range battles.

The issue is that poke characters thrive even better in close range while doing an insane amount of damage overall. And Marvel Rival's solution to that? Make dive characters assassinate in a way that's nearly impossible to react to UNLESS you swap to specific characters that in turn make it completely unplayable for them and to make healers do insane amount of healing such that if a team runs triple heals, nothing dies.

Then it comes to the teamups. These teamups have been made to address "weaknesses" of characters. Dive characters have teamups that increases their uptime, support characters have teamups that increase their healing output a ton or increase their self survivability a ton, brawl characters either have teamups that give them long range damage or massively increase their survivability, etc. etc. The issue is, characters NEED to have weaknesses for the game to be balanced and have an actual ecosystem.

The biggest additional issue is Marvel Rivals takes a VERY LONG time to address any characters being overbearingly OP. Devil Dinosaur has been a menace for multiple seasons causing it to be literally unplayable to play any tank other than Emma or Hood, when Phoenix melee tech was a thing (which allowed her to do more DPS than any melee characters at melee range) that was around for 4 months and terrorizing ranked play and pro play, Gambit has been a problem for over a year, the list goes on... 

TLDR: Everything needs a nerf and this game needs to stop powercreeping with every new unit.

Game Community:
People are miserable in this game. You play competitive to seek competitiveness, and every other game people are hard selling, are giga boosted from playing the overwhelming meta characters that come with terrible positioning and overall game macro, are giga boosted supports (I am saying this as a support main) and overall just very bigoted and egotistical people. People that then want to avoid those issues go to quickplay, and suddenly quickplay, a casual mode, becomes the sweatiest thing. You try to play someone you're new at and you will get flamed and harassed. People have massive egos and are unwilling to play something that would allow the team to win.

I think this largely is an issue with Marvel Rivals having been in this terrible state for so long.

Optimization:
This game is terribly optimized. While in OW I can get consistent 500 FPS, in Valorant I can get consistent 450 FPS, in this game I barely hold on to 180 and I get ping drops very often especially when a huge team fight happens. If you have a mid PC, you physically cannot play the game without installing configs which Netease has overall been incredibly inconsistent in what is bannable and what isn't.

Cosmetics:
This game compared to any other main shooter creates really great cosmetics at a very reasonable price. They also give plenty of currency for free to purchase skins if you are F2P. I do think the oversexualization of some skins can get overbearing, but most of them at the very least look very nice and pretty.

Visual Clutter:
Especially with the addition of every character having a new ability via teamups, this game can get insanely difficult to figure out what is going on. It doesn't help that Deadpool (and people who has his teamup) have abilities that is literally designed to make your screen even more cluttered.

===

The only reason I have this game installed still is to play with friends, which is very fun! But god forbid, if you are planning to play this game by yourself, RUN IMMEDIATELY. This game is very centered around catering to the casual playerbase, which is why most heroes are designed in a way to be incredibly strong. It is very cool to play your favorite superhero and beat people up with it! Until your favorite superhero is Iron Man and the enemy team has a Lord Spiderman named LuckyZeal with pimples all over his face and a Champion Hela to make the game unplayable for you.

Anyways, I don't think this game will ever address these issues. They have released patch notes for the next patch and they're largely just nothingburger nerfs and don't address the core issues with the gameplay loop. The main thing they did was reinforce triple heals with the patch notes, by also releasing a triple healer support character with Nightwalker. Nobody really wants to play tank because you're getting violated by Barnie half the time.

Playing with new people, learning the characters, finding my mains, getting steadily better and having fun running around as the different Marvel characters. 

Then I started to run into the usual suspects, the kind of people you see in competitive shooters in general. Taking the game way, way, way too seriously and being extremely rude. I get being angry during a game, I get frustrated and drop F bombs like anyone else... But making people cry because they had a bad game? That's too much. Getting an attitude before the match even starts? Not good. Throwing games because the only way you can find enjoyment in anything is to ruin it for everyone else? Grow up. And that's just in game. Interacting with the community in general has only gotten more and more toxic as the months and now years have gone by. 

For the 350+ hours in the back half of my playtime, I'm not exaggerating, were out of habit and because my gaming group defaulted to it over everything else. I wasn't enjoying it most of the time (tank main, suffering is a lifestyle we know well), and for every enjoyable game, I'd have a dozen that left me annoyed and in a worse mood. Even the casual game modes are infested with toxic players with overblown egos who think the opinions of a streamer are gospel and that the real problem with this game is that there are people who want to play it casually. 

It's a free to play team shooter with Marvel super heroes in it... It's not that serious. The thing about this that sucks is the gameplay is actually fun, I've got dozens of clips of crazy moments in this game and I've even saved full matches to watch back because of all the insane random things that happened. Now, for the last couple seasons the developers have made... Questionable design choices to say the least, so I can't even look at the gameplay and say "this at least feels good" anymore. Don't get me wrong, I do love certain aspects of this game. The art direction is beautiful, the characters and their kits are mainly fun to learn and I love how different each character is/can be used. 

However this game is such wasted potential. The power creep is actually insane, and the balancing is always lacking and never focusing on the ACTUAL issue, and instead altering something of the character's that doesn't actually fix the main problem with them. And some characters are ignored all together due to them simply not being in the META. Triple support is still a problem and is painful to play against especially in quick play and trying to learn a new character whilst being a higher level is genuinely just chinese water torture because over half the time you're fighting against a team with at least 2/3 champions who have over 250 hours on one character. And it's simply not fun to deal with; if it were ranked, then fine, it's ranked and it's competitive, but its quick play and it makes the game mode a drag. 

As a support player, I do hate how the strategist role is just slowly becoming heal bots, and when you do something that helps your team but isn't healing, you get told you're throwing. I love playing mantis and ultron and I love how different their kits are from the other healers, but I hate that they're simply not viable 90% of the time. And the power creep on supports specifically (cough cough luna invis cnd cough couch) is getting kinda insane. Luna does not need to match hela's damage, invis did not need a self shield that can save her all the time, and cloak and dagger did not need a point stalling invincible move. The ability for skill expression on characters is progressively lowered as every character has like 3 'get out of jail' cards and unfortunately it does make support a more braindead role since you don't really need to keep track of your cooldowns because odds are you already have another way out. 

I hope the team can properly sit down and assess what actually needs to change and properly implement it instead of buffing another character like phoenix or elsa just because they want them in the meta. They have talent, they just need to stop playing favourites.

hello this is my honest review of this game, It began innocently: a few matches after work, a couple of rounds with friends, a harmless curiosity about how Loki’s illusions or Magneto’s battlefield control worked. I told myself it was just another hero-shooter, something I’d pick up casually.
But Marvel Rivals is not casual. It is a vortex. A cosmic event. A multiversal black hole disguised as a game.
Within days, I wasn’t “playing matches”—I was studying team compositions like I was preparing for a doctoral thesis. I wasn’t “trying heroes”—I was optimizing builds at 3 a.m. while whispering, “One more match.”  My sleep schedule? Gone.
My productivity? Snapped like Thanos’ fingers.
My meals? Replaced by whatever I could eat with one hand while the other spammed abilities.
I started measuring time not in hours, but in respawn timers. I’d think, “I can do laundry in 12 seconds,” and then immediately queue for another match instead.  My chores formed a rebellion.
My inbox staged a coup.
My social life filed for emancipation.
Friends would ask, “Want to hang out?”
And I’d respond, “I can’t—I’m trying to master Scarlet Witch’s synergy combos.”
They stopped asking.  I began hearing ability voice lines in my sleep.
I started mentally assigning ultimate charge percentages to everyday tasks.
I caught myself thinking, “If I flank the kitchen from the left, I can reach the fridge faster.”
I tried to explain the game’s meta to my family. They nodded politely, the way people do when they realize someone has gone too deep. The turning point was when I opened the game intending to play “just one match,” and suddenly it was 2:47 a.m., my room was dark, my drink was warm, and I had somehow played 19 matches without blinking.
I stared at the screen and whispered, “Marvel Rivals… what have you done to me?” Because the game is too fun.
Because the hero abilities are too satisfying.
Because the team synergies are too clever.
Because every match feels like a Marvel movie fight scene I get to direct.
It didn’t ruin my life.
It ruined my free time.
And honestly? I let it.

I've been playing Marvel Rivals since Season 0 and have almost 2,000 hours in the game, so obviously I really enjoy it. But after playing for this long, there are definitely some things that I think need fixing.

The character balancing is probably my biggest issue. Sometimes you can spend hours learning a difficult character just to get beaten by someone playing a character that takes way less effort. Easier characters shouldn't be bad, but mastering harder characters should feel more rewarding.

Quick Play matchmaking can also be really frustrating. My team can be filled with people chilling or learning new characters while the other team feels like they're playing in a tournament. I don't expect every match to be perfectly balanced, but Quick Play should at least feel somewhat casual.

The reporting and surrender systems also need work. There's a difference between someone having a bad game and someone intentionally throwing. People who give up, sit in spawn, or purposely ruin matches should be dealt with more consistently. The surrender system also feels weird because people will try to surrender after one bad round, but when you're actually getting completely destroyed, somehow the vote doesn't pass.

Optimization has also gotten worse over time. I've noticed more stuttering, FPS drops, shader loading, and other performance issues after updates.

I'm also not a fan of the balloon system in the store. It feels too much like gacha. I'd rather just know exactly what I'm buying and how much I'm spending.

I've played since Season 0 and put almost 2,000 hours into this game because I genuinely enjoy it. I just hope they focus more on balancing, matchmaking, reporting, optimization, the surrender system, and keeping the store fair.

I really wanted to give this game a positive review because I do enjoy the core gameplay and when things go well, matches can be incredibly fun, dynamic and challenging. Though after over 10 seasons of gradually declining quality as well as new and longstanding issues getting ignored in favour of short-term cash grabs, matches feel more like torture instead of the fun challenge they used to be and the bleeding player count stands as an example of the state Rivals has sunken to. 

The game itself is heavily unoptimized, requiring relatively pricey gear to get any consistent performance out of it (I was able to run Cyberpunk2077 with relatively good stability on my older pc that I hadn't upgraded in years but had insane stuttering and frame drops even on low settings when playing Rivals). Now after upgrading my pc with relatively higher-end gear, I can now enjoy the pleasure of visual diarrhea constantly cluttering my screen while I try to find the enemy character model in a game of "Where's Waldo". Character balancing is a joke. where the aim of the game is which ult fight wins in the end leading to more effects spam. For a moment they seemed to be going in the right direction by nerfing the support ult frequency but then for every step forward, took two steps back and we're back to ults deciding fights again. 

One of the more infuriating things that has been placed into the game with intent, which makes it even more baffling that anyone thought it was a good idea, is the forced bot matches in quickplay. I have never met one person that said they enjoy being handed a free win in a game mode that you specifically pick to play with other PEOPLE. Because for the people who DO enjoy playing with bots- guess what?- you can play with bots by joining a BOT LOBBY. So WHY am I being forced to join in a bot match when I HAVEN'T selected the mode to PLAY WITH BOTS?? On top of that, because the bots throw themselves at you with all the grace of handsome squidward being shoved away from a falling shoe, the bot matches end up teaching and reinforcing BAD HABITS that cause you to lose more matches when playing against real players, making you lose even more and forcing MORE bot matches instead of you learning from your mistakes by being allowed to lose against real players without being treated with kid gloves and sent to the play pen to get a free win that means nothing whatsoever. 

This recent season (10) has been, in my mind, the most disastrous in terms of the goals of the developers. Instead of getting a new hero this season or any sort of tangible support for the game towards optimization, balancing or community management, we instead got a limited time brain-rotting, left click simulator team event that isn't even balanced for all the characters that are able to play it and is time-gated and scheduled during a time slot that a whole bunch of players in different countries are likely not going to be available to play it and a bunch of gatcha events for skins for the same handful of characters that always get them. With the amount of issues that have piled up over time, Rivals is going to need at least a season (likely more) to focus solely on the health of the game instead of how much they can milk it for if they want any chance of it surviving because from it's release, it showed the potential to be a strong compeditor for other hero shooters. I'd want it to be that way again and I'd even say that it has the potential to be that way again if they can manage to pull their heads out of their behinds and focus on something that doesn't squeeze players for as much money and time as possible.

Why? My impression is that banning paying customers isn't a priority when those same players are buying skins and generating revenue.

Now let's talk about performance.

You could have one of the best gaming PCs available and still struggle with terrible FPS unless you enable frame generation. The optimization is embarrassing for a competitive game where performance and responsiveness should be priorities.

And then there's matchmaking, arguably the worst part of the entire game.

This is a team-based competitive game, yet the matchmaking makes absolutely no sense.

You can reach the top three competitive ranks and still regularly encounter players who have no business being there. Spider-Man mains going 4–20 while blaming their supports, DPS players finishing entire matches with zero or two final hits, and teammates who seemingly have no understanding of basic teamwork.

How do these players reach some of the highest ranks in the game?

And if you're in the lower ranks, good luck. You get matched with players who lack basic game knowledge, while the matchmaking feels designed to keep you trapped in an endless cycle of winning and losing. Lose five matches, win five matches, and finish the season exactly where you started.

Whether this is intentional or simply the result of a fundamentally broken matchmaking system, the outcome is the same: an exhausting ranked experience that rewards grinding more than actual skill.

The biggest problem is the game's priorities.

Instead of meaningfully addressing toxicity, improving optimization, fixing matchmaking, and making competitive play fair, Marvel Rivals seems far more interested in releasing skins and finding new ways to monetize its player base.

There is so much potential here, and that's what makes the current state of the game even more disappointing. After 1,500 hours, I've watched a promising competitive game turn into an increasingly frustrating experience.

Marvel Rivals doesn't need more skins, empty promises, or cosmetic updates. It needs developers who prioritize fixing the actual game.

Until that happens, it feels like the only message the developers want players to hear is:

"BUY OUR SKINS. GIVE US YOUR MONEY. WE'LL PROMISE TO FIX THE GAME LATER."

OVERVIEW
With ~2,000 hours on this game between pc and console since season 0 and peaking at C1 I've put a lot of time into playing across a variety of roles and ranks. Love the general concept of the game, the art style, the skins, the gameplay mechanisms, and character abilities. However, there are consistent problems across platforms and ranks that have fatigued and possibly ended my enjoyment of the game.

1. Smurfing
Regardless of amount of obvious smurfs I've encountered (low level accounts with 80%+ win rates) stacked or unstacked, this game does not have a proper system in place to deal with the constant barrage of these accounts heavily skewing match quality across all ranks. I've experienced it at it's worst this season (10 / 10.5) where on average 50% of my matches have been determined by which team has the smurf / smurfs as the remaining players don't have the skill set / game sense to match. This could be resolved with stricter account creation requirements, better placement match ranking, increasing rank points allocated for atypical win streaks / win rate so accounts get to their appropriate rank faster, or a stricter ban policy towards smurf accounts. 

2. Toxicity and Cheating
This community is one of the worst online gaming communities I've ever experienced and I'm no stranger to online games. It feels like a symptom of poor policy around how these accounts are handled. Around 25% of my matches are determined by which team has a thrower (not just having a bad game, but actively not playing, rage quitting, team pick banning, intentionally dying, or using abilities in a hostile manner like jeff ulting own team off map). Bans have seemed to become more frequent when I report, but they are rarely long enough for repeat offenders or they hop on their multiple alt accounts and continue the cycle. Surely there's a better way to handle this or be more strict on thrower or toxic teammates. Cheating reporting seems to have improved as well, but in game detection is often slow or inconsistent. I've rarely had cheaters kicked from an active match I'm in, usually it's after the fact (hours / days, never, etc). 

3. Balance
Time to kill has become unbearably fast in season 10 / 10.5 due to the balance philosophy being buff centered instead of nerfing overpowered characters. There's also bad kit design that provides very little character interaction that is consistently unfun to play against, ex: Black Panther / Spider Man / Black Cat. I don't have an expectation for perfect balance, but it should be relatively balanced with regular balance patches to provide more flexibility to viable team comp selection. 

4. Matchmaking
Although the game doesn't use a matchmaking model called EOMM, matchmaking uses an algorithm called EnMatch that is engagement based and creates unfun patterns of long win / loss streaks that are less typical in other matchmaking algorithms. The algorithm white paper can be found under: EnMatch: Matchmaking for Better Player Engagement via Neural Combinatorial Optimization. It creates matches that are much more statistically skewed to provided a win or loss based on large discrepancies in aggregate team capability for the players on each team. It's extremely difficult to offset a match that's statistically designed to be a loss or win with near flawless or terrible play. Games with an even playing field are more exciting and fun! There will still be the occasional stomp due to lack of compatibility of teammates in other systems, but it won't be nearly as skewed.  

Either way. Hoping NetEase takes these repeating themes seriously as I'd love for this game to thrive. For now, I'm going to dial back my time on this game and reassess as new seasons are released. Will update if the status quo changes while I'm still actively playing.

[h2]I love this game, but there are some things that needs fixing.[/h2]
 
This is by far the WORST experience I had on a hero shooters game. and no I'm not gonna talk about how the community is horrible even though that is part of my complain but here are some takes I have for this game.

[h2]The imbalance between characters.[/h2] 

You can have someone play the hardest character to master and still can be bested by a character that only needs to hold a button. I'm not claiming to be a skilled player myself, but even I can recognize when a game fails to properly reward skill and mastery. Instead of encouraging players to learn, improve, and master more challenging characters, the current balance makes it feel like the game favors those who put in less effort and gives them little reason to get better.

[h2]Their new approach on their store page.[/h2]

I have mixed feelings about the store. I don't mind the bundle discounts or event passes that require you to actually play the game and earn points. Those at least reward players for their time and effort.

But the balloon mechanic? That's just pure gacha.

The discounts make you feel like you're getting a better deal, but that's exactly how gacha mechanics pull you in. They make you feel like you're getting closer to the reward, so you keep spending your hard earned units because you've already invested so much. And with the balloons being limited-time, there's even more pressure to keep going before the opportunity disappears.

Before you know it, you're spending more than you originally intended, not necessarily because the reward is worth it, but because you've already spent too much to walk away empty handed. It's that [b] "I'm already so close, I can't stop now"[/b]  mentality that makes these mechanics so predatory. 

[h2]The Quick Play Matchmaking System.[/h2]

This one is a little harder to explain because I'm not sure whether I'm simply unlucky or if the matchmaking system follows some sort of formula that I'm unaware of.

Whenever I queue for Quick Play, I often end up with the usual players who are experimenting with characters they haven't mastered yet, learning new abilities, or simply playing casually. And honestly, there's nothing wrong with that. It's Quick Play, after all.

The problem is when the opposing team suddenly has what feels like an entire NBA roster of highly experienced players, complete with Lord icons and insane plays, while my team struggles to secure even a single elimination.

It creates a frustrating imbalance where one team seems to be playing casually, while the other looks like they're competing in a tournament. I'm not expecting every match to be perfectly balanced, but when the skill gap is so enormous that one team can barely fight back, it stops being an enjoyable experience.

[b] Quick Play should be a place where players can relax, experiment, and improve without feeling like they're being thrown into a competitive match against players leagues above their level. [/b]  Whether this is simply bad luck or an issue with the matchmaking system itself, the inconsistency makes the experience frustrating.

[h2] The Reporting System. [/h2]
Initially, I was going to make a separate section for Ranked matchmaking, but honestly, I don't have nearly as many issues with Ranked itself outside of players who deliberately throw games or smurf.

What frustrates me more is the reporting system. I've submitted countless reports against players who give up the moment a match starts going badly, whether it's because we struggle to capture the objective or because they're repeatedly dying and not receiving enough healing. Instead of adapting, working with the team, or trying a different approach, some players simply decide the game is no longer worth playing and proceed to sit at spawn or deliberately misused their abilities and ruin the experience for everyone else.

Yet, despite the number of reports I've submitted, it feels like [b] only 1 out of every 10 reports actually results in punishment, while the rest appear to go unanswered.[/b]

I understand that not every report will necessarily result in disciplinary action, and that the developers need to review each case before deciding whether a player has violated the rules. However, when players can repeatedly sabotage matches or deliberately throw games with seemingly little consequence, it raises questions about how effective the reporting system actually is.

And to be clear, [b] poor performance is not the same as throwing. [/b] A player who repeatedly dies, misses their shots, struggles to secure eliminations, or fails to receive enough healing isn't necessarily sabotaging the game. Everyone has bad matches, and not everyone has the same level of skill. These are things that happen naturally in a team-based game.

[h2] The Surrender Option in Ranked. [/h2]
Finally, a small complaint that shouldn't require too many words, right? Wrong.

The surrender system feels just as frustrating as the reporting system, albeit for a different reason. Sometimes, a player performs poorly in the first round and immediately calls for a surrender before the second round has even started. The match isn't necessarily lost, yet the moment things don't go their way, they'd rather give up than try to turn things around.

However, the opposite problem exists, too. There are matches where the majority of the team agrees that the game is no longer realistically winnable, yet the match continues because the surrender system allows the few players who disagree, or haven't voted at all, to prevent it from passing.

I'm not saying every difficult match should end in a surrender. Comebacks happen, and sometimes it's worth fighting until the end. But there should be a reasonable balance between preventing players from giving up too early and allowing the majority of the team to end a match when continuing serves little purpose.

[b] A surrender system should neither encourage players to give up at the slightest disadvantage nor force an entire team to continue a miserable match because of a small minority.[/b] There needs to be a better way to account for the team's overall decision without making surrendering feel either too easy or practically impossible.

[h2] The Game's Optimization [/h2]
I can't speak for the game's earlier versions, as I only started playing around Season 8 or 8.5. However, from Season 9 onward, I've noticed a clear decline in the game's optimization.

With each passing season, the overall performance seems to have gotten worse rather than improved. To see a game become increasingly demanding or perform less smoothly over time, especially when optimization is something that is needed in a competitive hero shooter game.

With practically every patch, the shaders have to reload, and performance issues start creeping in. Lag, stuttering, and severe frame drops become increasingly noticeable, sometimes to the point where the game is practically unplayable. Instead of being able to jump into a match and enjoy the game, I'm left dealing with performance issues that seem to resurface with every update.

[h2] What can they do? [/h2]
- Reward skill, not just ease of use
- Make casual games feel casual, Improve skill-based matchmaking
- Distinguish intentional throwing from poor performance
- Fix surrender system for both extremes
- Stop performance from deteriorating with every patch
- Make purchases transparent and fair

That is all.

With nearly 1,000 hours, I feel I have played this game enough to leave an honest review.

Simply put, this game is amazing.

There are hiccups here an there, some bad dev decisions, etc. But here's the thing, EVERY LIVE SERVICE GAME WILL HAVE THESE ISSUES, and to date, this game has the LEAST worrisome issues of all the competitive games I've played. The vast majority of people leaving negative reviews have not analyzed their thoughts before posting. The biggest issues with this game come entirely from the playerbase, something that the devs have little to no control over. Sure, I heavily disagree with some balance changes, but THAT'S WHAT BALANCE CHANGES ARE FOR! They're meant to keep the game changing with fresh content. If they kept my mains overpowered, it would get stale very quickly. Likewise, if they kept them too weak, I'd be more upset than if the characters fluctuated in strength, which they do.

Seldom have I played a game where the entire roster is viable. There have been changed made that, frankly, make the game very unfun. This isn't even about the truly awful Thanos event (Though that definitely deserves to be mentioned given the timing) but rather, two specific things that have slowly but surely punished their most ardent players:

1. Match Making Punishes Good Players:
   So, if you happen to be good or even great at the game, the matchmaking punishes you. If you can't help but notice it feels like either you are the only person on your team that seems to be doing well, OR you haven't seen anyone else carry the game on your side lately, that means that YOU are victim to this. Basically, instead of trying to keep the general skill level even among the team, it will pull specifically well performing players and pair them up with people on massive lose streaks or consistently underperforming to increase their chances to win. The result of this, instead, "rewards" trolls who are just messing around and never had an interest to win by bringing in some poor sucker into a doomed game, effectively punishing players that do okay by purposefully giving them terrible teammates.

   This wasn't a problem with the earlier seasons, so I don't understand why they thought they needed to fix this now. Every team had an equal mix of Unemployed God-Tier DPS or Spiderman Death Montage Fisher on both sides. It felt a lot more random. This was probably done in an attempt to fix that, bur frankly, this is so much worse. You don't even need to be Celestial to feel this, it's literally in Quick Play too, and it just makes your biggest fans (The people who spend the most time in this game and actually get okay at it) feel like their game quality has gone down, and that's because it HAS. 

2. Console Players Now Have Weird Advantages:
    This one kinda baffles me. Most games separate the PC and Console community in shooter games for good reason: The PC players are far far more accurate and can perform leagues better than console players who are limited by joy-stick aiming and movement. This, usually, makes it very unfair for the console players and so even the playerbase wants a hard separation (See games like Apex Legends). But, it is a bit different in this game. They don't separate them at all. Console players get some tools to even the playing field like a auto-aim so they don't need to actually aim nearly as well. This is, actually fine. It's still generally not as good as mouse and keyboard (You can circle strafe around console players at close range and see the blatantly crutch as they literally cannot turn fast enough) and while it was always annoying to have a bunch of console players on your team, they changed something...

   I don't even know how to describe it. It's like some kind of input correction? Basically, just because you are aiming and shooting at a console player as a PC player now, if they aren't there on the CONSOLE player's side, then that shot misses. You, as the PC player, could have spot on aim and still miss now. It's kinda insane. This definitely wasn't a problem before, and I don't know why it's here now, but it successfully flipped the paradigm and now console players get so much hand-holding benefits that it's actually more to your advantage to have as many console players on your team as possible. 

This is, obviously, pretty awful if you value your own time as a PC player since you are actively punished for having good aim. This shouldn't be the case in any shooter ever, and it's insane that they decided to do this. This being a review on Steam, it should reflect in the reviews for PC players, and honestly if you do play this on PC, you should be rightfully pissed.

Marvel Rivals is a game that started off as a breath of fresh air and rapidly devolved into a suffocating toxic wasteland.
What began as an incredibly fun, fast-paced hero shooter has quickly been ruined by a total failure to manage the game's health. You will face catastrophic, world-ending threats in every single match. Unfortunately, those threats are not Thanos. They are just an unholy mix of broken matchmaking, high-rank smurfs, and an explosion of unpunished aimbots.

The Matchmaking: Perfectly Unbalanced

• The Daycare Protocol: The system regularly pairs one high-ranked solo player with four toddlers chewing on their controllers. You are not playing a hero shooter. You are running an underfunded daycare in a war zone.
• The Forced Cooldown: If you accidentally win two games in a row, the algorithm panics and throws you into a woodchipper of Top 500 sweatlords while your teammates play via a Smart Fridge.

Ranked Mode: The Grand Delusion

• The Smurf Invasion: Low-tier ranked lobbies are entirely compromised by Top 500 players who get bored of their own queue times. They create fresh accounts to ruthlessly stomp casual players for sport, turning Bronze to Diamond games into an absolute slaughterhouse.
• Bloated Tiers: Thanks to an ELO system that aggressively hands out points for wins while barely scratching you for losses, the actual ranks are hopelessly bloated. Gold is the new Bronze, and Celestial is just Platinum with a massive ego.
• The Spreadsheet Meta: Competitive integrity is non-existent because sweaty stacks use third-party trackers to ban your favorite hero before the gates even open. You lose to an Excel spreadsheet rather than superior strategy.

The Cheater Uptick: Peak Tactical Apathy

• The Hitlist: Aimbots and wallhacks have turned specific hitscans into literal boss fights. You will regularly face a Hawkeye who never misses a pixel, a Punisher whose turret tracks at the speed of sound, and a Luna Snow who lands every single ice shard into your skull through solid geometry.
• The Floor-Freezing Idol: Even when the Luna Snow players aren't hacking, the game does the cheating for them. Her freeze ability has a hitbox the size of a small planet. She can literally stare directly at the linoleum floor, panic-throw her ability, and still flash-freeze you from three meters away.
• Band-Aid Solutions: NetEase promising to refund your rank points after a hacker destroys you feels like a doctor offering a plaster after letting a grizzly bear maul you in the waiting room. They are far too busy selling cosmetic bundles to fix competitive integrity.

The Verdict

The launch window honeymoon phase is officially over. Come for the stunning cel-shaded visuals, stay because a Top 500 smurf or an aimbotting Punisher has pinned you inside your spawn door while Luna Snow freezes your ankles by looking at the dirt.
Rating: 2/10 Floor-Aimed Blizzards.

Honestly, Apex Legends has given me so many fun moments.
